cards.title: Reading the map
items: Six regions group real responsibilities; repeated tools/swarm.mjs labels identify separate functions/commands in the same module, not services.
SRC references pin the inspected repository commit. Arrows mean the labeled call, read, write or artifact flow; disconnected maintenance commands are independently invoked.

The orchestrator reviews and invokes integrate/ship; run never automatically approves its own output. go supplies callbacks for selected stages; its internal implementation is outside supplied context.

cards.title: Inputs and hard gates
items: Manifest version 1; 1–256 jobs; concurrency 1–32 (default 2). context/outputs are explicit arrays of at most 100 files. contract must be in every context and no output.

Model is mandatory. tier is optional metadata, never model routing; expensive requires tierReason. Unknown fields, unsafe paths, symlinks, missing/empty context and within-manifest writer collisions refuse.

validate/preflight probe check interpreters/modules. context-check performs bounded static matching: detected uncovered references refuse with suggestedIgnoreTests; directory/registry drift remains advisory.

API total declared context is capped at 200,000 bytes; each inlined file is truncated at 60,000 bytes and recorded in contextInlined. maxOutputTokens accepts 256–32,768; outputs × 500 > explicit cap refuses.

Public-repo prompt/contract private-term check depends on configured terms and GitHub visibility lookup. Private-data path matches require privateData:true. maxCredits requires a readable preflight cost total within cap.

cards.title: Run lifecycle and disk
items: Run claim is an exclusive wx file; live board is a separate per-user registry keyed by shared git directory. It detects matching live output claims; it is not a transactional file-reservation service.
All job inputs are snapshotted before workers launch; base hashes and modes underpin integrate conflicts. after waits for complete predecessors and copies only changed outputs; Codex rejects after.
Copied workspaces hold selected files. Codex and Claude shell instead get detached HEAD worktrees, resources and copied skills. Root uncommitted edits are not automatically part of HEAD.

CLI progress samples stdout/stderr counters and timestamps, not useful-work or GPU activity. API calls return only when settled. Cancellation markers reach the owner, which terminates process groups or aborts fetch.

The run stores message.txt, provider.jsonl, stderr.log, response.txt, state and invalid-envelope evidence. Failed CLI processes add agent.log. privateData withholds response.txt and agent.log; it is not a claim that every provider log is erased.

cards.title: Skills, toolchains and feedback
items: skillsDir (often coordination/skills) overrides config skills.dir; full tree copies into .swarm/skills. Named skills override path matching; every known skill is indexed, attached bodies are prepended.
Estimated skill tokens = ceil(chars/4): >800 warns, >1200 refuses. Attached skill resultKeys conflicts can refuse dispatch; filesMustChange/resultKeys are checked before integration writes.
env and gotchas prefer the selected root, then the main worktree. Env denies reserved and secret-looking keys. env --print also materializes .swarm/bin/git with stash/unsafe-restore guards.
ports.mjs hashes the worktree path, skips the Vite HMR block, probes the base port and tries up to 50 blocks; it does not reserve or prove all ten ports free.
Coordinator-authored lessons become .swarm/gotchas.md or a --evidence failures block for the next prompt. There is no automatic agent-log→lessons writer in the inspected code.

cards.title: What the adapters can actually do
items: Claude file-tools mode: restricted/safe flags, empty MCP, no Chrome or Bash. It cannot execute tests. web:true adds WebSearch/WebFetch only to read-only jobs. File-tool scope is not an OS sandbox.

Claude shell: macOS sandbox-exec around the entire CLI, Bash plus file tools, dedicated worker key, scrubbed environment, job-scoped HOME and scratch outside repositories. setup executes first in the parent, outside this sandbox.

Claude shell internet access is through a localhost CONNECT proxy allowing api.anthropic.com:443 only. Own loopback tests are allowed; existing listening ports are denied unless explicit loopbackAllow is used. Nonempty networkAllow is refused.

Codex: sandbox-exec around codex exec with explicit -m, ephemeral session and last-message file. Can execute tests. The outer profile restricts files but does not deny network; do not apply Claude shell's network policy to it.

Codex grants its tree, git metadata, selected caches and scratch. Declared output copy-back remains the integration boundary; fallback results retain the tree. Codex never propagates missing outputs as deletes.

Hermes/Qwen have no file/shell tools, one turn and strict terminal JSONL; tool activity is rejected. API models have no tools, filesystem, browsing, image viewing or tests; only the parent performs transport and file writes.

cards.title: Result handling and provider policy
items: Codex resolves the last fenced/top-level object, then rereads the result file, then checks dirty declared outputs; fallback or invalid envelopes retain worktree evidence.

Plain Claude retries one transient 5xx/429 api_error in the kept workspace. A separate unparsable JSON-demand reply can receive one same-session re-ask. Claude shell is excluded from both unsandboxed paths.

API envelopes require every output exactly once as files or edits. find must match exactly once. Invalid structured envelopes retain response-invalid.txt. No shell or arbitrary output path is accepted.

OpenRouter enforces data_collection:deny; anthropic/* pins Anthropic without fallback; deepseek/* is bookkeeping-only. Pricing must be available and estimated request spend must fit $5/job and $25/day.

OpenRouter alone may retry empty length truncation once at twice the token limit after cap recheck. This is bounded retry, not a guarantee of exactly one HTTP request or a transactional spend reservation.
Provider-reported costs remain distinct from rates.mjs transcript estimates. Unreported costs stay null, with costNotReported; model mismatch warns rather than failing the job.

cards.title: Review and integration exceptions
items: inspect compares base/current/proposed hashes and modes, lists blocked/missing/conflicting/ready files, and shows warnings and reported costs. --results prefers declared resultFile with parse/schema disagreement warnings.

integrate requires an acceptable completed run by default, acquires .swarm/integration.lock and verifies metadata, outputs, base hashes/modes, skill checks, deviations and dropped writes before writes.

--accept-blocked, --salvage, --accept-deviation, --accept-dropped and --salvage-dropped are explicit exceptions. The latter can recover saved undeclared writes; ordinary integration copies declared outputs.
Explicit deletes allow removal of existing outputs; absent-from-base-and-proposal outputs instead warn output-never-written. Codex's own output collector remains stricter and refuses missing files.

integrateRun has jobs/privateNamesFile parameters, but the inspected CLI does not parse/forward them for integrate. Its private-name scan is conditional on the direct parameter and limited to shared/, fixtures/, tests/. Ship has the wired CLI private-name gate.

Writes are followed by preChecks on every integration, then checks, then optional mutants on a green base. Checks failure does not roll files back; CLI exits nonzero by default. Partial write-stage failures are marked retryable.

cards.title: Checks and ship gates
items: run performs a base check before dispatch; red base needs explicit acceptance/reason except the recorded auto-accept case where all identified failing locations are owned outputs.

runChecks classifies cannot-run/spawn-error/unrunnable separately, retries after preChecks once, and may compare failures with base. Mutants validate before writes and restore bytes in finally; redcheck tests against base while retaining tests.

ship requires integrated state for RUN or the selected checked-out branch for --branch, committed tracked files, parsed PR payload, resolved gh/git, pre-push content guards, appropriate lock/build checks, and rerun local checks.

The PR body's <!-- swarm:checks --> is replaced by check evidence. Missing/blank/leftover required sections refuse before push. Proven pre-existing failures yield held-red-check unless --accept-pre-existing.

After git push, gh api creates/updates the PR; CI must settle for the exact head SHA. no-ci, timeout or failing checks cannot merge. Limited flaky reruns distinguish changed tests from untouched/platform-only failures.

After green CI, first nonblank body line starting **needs holds for owner review and prints Changed/Could break/Proof. --no-merge returns ready. Otherwise gh pr merge pins the SHA, rereads MERGED and may wait for a release tag.

cards.title: Auxiliary commands and installation
items: doctor probes compatibility/configuration, optional local health; onboard renders readiness guidance. Neither is model-access proof. next --from reads a queued ticket hint; skills check validates frontmatter; help lists usage.

ask runs one read-only job; scout enables Claude web research and normalizes a license-gated report; sweep fetches gh/API candidates first, gates metadata in code and asks Claude to rank. Sweep's observed-cost threshold skips future areas, not in-flight ones.

verify --orb dispatch is visible, but tools/verify-orb.mjs is outside supplied context. agent-log is not a recognized tools/swarm.mjs command at this revision; per-job agent.log is the verified evidence path.

installUser snapshots tools/package/skill references to versions/<version>-<hash8>, atomically repoints current and keeps the newest five plus current. Active-version retention across repeated pruning is not guaranteed.

installProject writes .project-swarm.json, registry, missing coordination seeds, delimited agent pointers and .gitignore. update fetches and validates release tags then installs; update --projects requires --yes before pointer/backup changes.

packaging-check is used by validate/integrate/ship, not by installUser. check-pins independently compares Python/npm exact pins and vendored metadata. No install→preflight or install→check-pins call is asserted.
